brief: Snow (#45, `snowCover`, `snowAt(x,y,t)` at ~1011) and foot wear (`wear[]`, written at ~1822 by every walker step, read by `drawGround` at ~3388 for desire paths) do not know each other: a lying cover whitens the lawn evenly and the town's most-loved emergent feature — the paths people wear — vanishes for a quarter of the year. `snowAt` already takes less on trodden KINDS; extend that to the wear VALUE so a worn line through the lawn stays dark through the snow and a fresh cover is re-trodden from the arches inward over a morning. Then give the pre-dawn sweeper (~2320, `sweeper`) a winter job: the strip they sweep (their actual route) is cleared, so at dawn on a snowy day there is one swept path and the rest is white until feet cut the desire paths again.
successLooksLike: A winter-morning shot (seed 7, snowCover > 0.4) shows dark desire paths through a white lawn and one swept strip; the same instant on HEAD is an even white. Summer frames byte-identical to HEAD. A probe over five seed-winters: mean snow on cells with wear > 0.45 is under half the mean on cells with wear < 0.1. snow-year.mjs's cover means move less than 5%.
avoid: Do not add a new ground kind or a new R() draw. Wear is per courtyard cell only — do not invent wear for the paved east. Keep the repaint on SNOW_REPAINT steps; a per-frame ground redraw is the one thing that would fail perf.
